title: Larger fish can sprint faster but cover similar distances and tire more slowly

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Larger fish can sprint faster but cover similar distances and tire more slowly

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Since muscular work available scales as the cube of linear size while the rate of energy supply, depending on respiratory surface, scales only as the square, a larger fish should achieve a much higher burst speed than a smaller one but travel a similar distance over a year, and smaller individuals should fatigue faster and have less staying power.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: the singular result ought to follow that, in swimming for instance, the larger fish ought to be able to put on a spurt of speed far in excess of the smaller one; but the distance travelled by the year’s end should be very much alike for both of them.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter II, “On Magnitude”; topic “Energy supply and fatigue”. Scope: similar, closely related animals of different size, especially swimming fish

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch02-05: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.54

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The predictions are explicit and can be tested for selected species, but the required performance and long-term movement variables are fragmented. A small team could resolve individual components, not the full joint scaling claim.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Within closely related fishes, regress burst speed, fatigue time and annual movement distance on body length while controlling temperature and ecology, and compare exponents with the square-cube predictions. Larger fish lacking higher burst speed, or annual distance increasing strongly with size, would refute components of the claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Temperature, swimming mode and tag effects confound size comparisons.

Burst speed and fatigue are rarely paired with annual tracking in the same individuals.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.6
data adequacy: 0.35
operationalizability: 0.85
analysis feasibility: 0.45
data existence: 0.45

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Burst speed, annual distance, and fatigue are well-defined variables, and the three-part scaling is discriminating if they are measured together within a species. What exists openly is mostly telemetry of larger individuals and uneven species-level speeds, so the joint size series has to be compiled from experimental papers. That supports a partial test, not a direct resolution of the full prediction.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Within similar fish, fit burst speed, distance covered over a year, and time to fatigue against length. The claim predicts a steep rise of burst speed with length, little change in annual distance, and faster fatigue in smaller fish; a flat burst speed or an annual distance that scales like burst speed would count against it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Sprint tests, fatigue curves, and annual tracks are rarely available for the same size series.

Reynolds number, temperature, and body shape change with size and can mimic the predicted exponents.

fields.value:

operationalizability: 0.7
analysis feasibility: 0.4
data existence: 0.45
discriminating power: 0.55
